Visioner BIG | 🇫🇮 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ Finland suspects a Russian military helicopter of violating its airspace, penetrating more than four kilometers into Finnish territory just hours after a drone attack on a Russian cargo vessel in the Baltic Sea. According to Le Monde, citing Finland’s Ministry of Defense, the suspected airspace violation occurred shortly after a Russian cargo ship was targeted by unmanned aerial vehicles in the Baltic region. Finnish authorities are examining the incident, although the helicopter’s mission and any connection to the earlier maritime attack remain unclear. The suspected intrusion adds another layer of tension to the increasingly sensitive security environment in the Baltic Sea. Any confirmed violation of Finnish airspace by Russian military aircraft would raise concerns for NATO, particularly amid attacks on Russian maritime assets. The timing is notable, but there is currently no established evidence linking the helicopter’s movements to the drone strike. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet
